questions.stem_en: A company uses AWS Organizations with all features enabled. Workload accounts are in an OU named Workloads, and new accounts are added to that OU every month. The company must prevent every IAM user and role in those accounts, including each account's root user, from using AWS services outside two approved Regions. Administrators of each account must not be able to remove the restriction. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices_en.text: Create an SCP with a Deny statement for requests outside the two approved Regions, and attach it to the Workloads OU.
Create an IAM policy that denies requests outside the two approved Regions, and attach it to every IAM user and role in each workload account.
Create an SCP with a Deny statement for requests outside the two approved Regions, and attach it to the management account.
Set a permissions boundary that allows only the two approved Regions on every IAM role in the workload accounts, and check new accounts each month.

explanation.summary: SCP はメンバーアカウントの IAM ユーザーとロール（ルートユーザーも含む）の権限を制限し、OU に付けた Deny はその下のすべてのアカウントに効きます。後から OU に入ったアカウントにも効き、アカウントの IAM の権限では SCP を超えられません。

per_choice.A: 正しい。OU の Deny は配下のすべてのアカウントとルートユーザーに効き、新しいアカウントにも自動で効きます。
per_choice.B: アカウントごとの IAM ポリシーは、そのアカウントの管理者が外せます。ルートユーザーにも付けられず、新しいアカウントごとの作業も要ります。
per_choice.C: SCP は管理アカウントのユーザーやロールには効かず、メンバーアカウントにだけ効くため、ワークロードのアカウントを制限できません。
per_choice.D: ロールにしか効かずルートユーザーは制限できず、アカウントの管理者が外せます。毎月の確認の手間もかかります。

references.quote: An SCP restricts permissions for IAM users and roles in member accounts, including the member account's root user.
when they are applied at the root or the OU-level they affect all the accounts under it.
SCPs don't affect users or roles in the management account. They affect only the member accounts in your organization.

questions.stem_en: In a company's organization, the root has the FullAWSAccess SCP. An OU named Sandbox has FullAWSAccess removed and instead has an SCP that allows only Amazon S3 and Amazon EC2 actions. A member account in the Sandbox OU has FullAWSAccess attached. A developer in that account has an IAM policy that allows all Amazon DynamoDB actions, but every DynamoDB request is denied. What should a DevOps engineer do to allow the developer to use DynamoDB with the LEAST change to the organization?

choices_en.text: Attach a new IAM policy to the developer that explicitly allows all DynamoDB actions on all resources.
Attach an SCP that allows DynamoDB actions directly to the member account.
Add the DynamoDB actions to the Allow statement of the SCP that is attached to the Sandbox OU.
Attach an SCP that allows DynamoDB actions to the management account of the organization.

explanation.summary: SCP で許されるには、ルートからアカウントまでの経路のすべての段（各 OU とアカウント自身）に明示的な Allow が要ります。Sandbox OU の SCP が DynamoDB を許していないため、IAM ポリシーで許していても拒否されます。

per_choice.A: IAM ポリシーは既に許しています。SCP で許されていないアクションは、IAM ポリシーで許しても実行できません。
per_choice.B: アカウントの段はすでに FullAWSAccess で許しています。Sandbox OU の段に Allow が無いので拒否されたままです。
per_choice.C: 正しい。経路の中で Allow が欠けている Sandbox OU の段に DynamoDB を足せば、すべての段で許されます。
per_choice.D: SCP は管理アカウントのユーザーやロールには効かず、メンバーアカウントの評価の経路にも入らないため、変わりません。

references.quote: there must be an explicit Allow statement at every level from the root through each OU in the direct path to the account (including the target account itself).
If a user or role has an IAM permission policy that grants access to an action that is either not allowed or explicitly denied by the applicable SCPs, the user or role can't perform that action.

questions.stem_en: A company is adopting a third-party monitoring service that runs in the vendor's AWS account and serves many customers. The service needs to read metrics from the company's AWS account. The company does not want to give the vendor long-term credentials and wants to prevent the confused deputy problem. Which actions should a DevOps engineer take to meet these requirements? (Choose TWO.)

choices_en.text: Create an IAM role with read permissions for metrics, and in its trust policy allow the vendor's account and require the external ID that the vendor provides for the company.
Ask the vendor to specify the company's external ID in every AssumeRole API call that it makes for the company's role.
Create an IAM user with read permissions for metrics, and give the vendor an access key that is rotated every 90 days.
Create an IAM role whose trust policy allows the vendor's account without any condition, and rely on the vendor to restrict which customer data it reads.
Create an SCP that allows the vendor's account to read metrics, and attach it to the company's account.

explanation.summary: 外部 ID の主な役目は混乱した代理の問題を防ぐことで、ロールの信頼ポリシーに指定し、AssumeRole の呼び出しで毎回指定します。ロールを引き受けさせれば、ベンダーに長期の認証情報を渡さずに済みます。

per_choice.A: 正しい。信頼ポリシーで外部 ID を必須にすると、会社用の外部 ID を示した時だけロールを引き受けられます。
per_choice.B: 正しい。外部 ID は AssumeRole の呼び出しで常に指定するものとされています。
per_choice.C: アクセスキーは長期の認証情報で、ローテーションしても要件に反します。
per_choice.D: ロールで長期の認証情報は避けられますが、外部 ID が無いと混乱した代理の問題を防げません。
per_choice.E: SCP は権限を与えないため、ベンダーにアクセスを許すことはできません。

references.quote: The primary function of the external ID is to address and prevent The confused deputy problem.
You must specify this ID when you define the trust policy for the role.
You should always specify the external ID in your AssumeRole API calls.
No permissions are granted by an SCP.

questions.stem_en: In a member account, developers must be able to create IAM roles for their AWS Lambda functions. A platform team in the same account must keep its full administrative permissions. The security team requires that any role a developer creates can never have permissions beyond a defined set, even if the developer attaches a broader policy to it. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices_en.text: Attach an SCP to the member account that limits all IAM principals in the account to the defined set of permissions.
Create a managed policy for the defined set, and allow developers to create roles only when that policy is set as the role's permissions boundary.
Attach an RCP to the member account that limits the permissions of roles that developers create.
Allow developers to create roles freely, and have the security team review each new role's policies every week.

explanation.summary: permissions boundary は管理ポリシーで、アイデンティティベースのポリシーがエンティティに与えられる最大の権限を決めます。開発者が作るロールに境界を必須にすれば、広いポリシーを付けても境界を超えられず、プラットフォームチームには影響しません。

per_choice.A: SCP はアカウントのすべてのユーザーとロールの上限になるため、プラットフォームチームの管理者権限まで制限されます。
per_choice.B: 正しい。開発者が作るロールだけに上限が付き、プラットフォームチームの権限は変わりません。
per_choice.C: RCP は、組織の外のプリンシパルが組織のリソースへアクセスするのを制限するためのもので、開発者が作るロールの権限の上限にはなりません。
per_choice.D: 確認するまでの間、範囲を超えた権限を持つロールが使えてしまい、要件を満たしません。

references.quote: A permissions boundary is an advanced feature for using a managed policy to set the maximum permissions that an identity-based policy can grant to an IAM entity.
SCPs offer central control over the maximum available permissions for the IAM users and IAM roles in your organization.
Use an RCP when you need to restrict IAM principals that are external to your organization accounts making requests to access resources within your organization’s member accounts.
